title: Russian forces seize Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant
body:
On 4 March 2022, the ninth day of the invasion, Russian forces seized the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in south-eastern Ukraine during heavy fighting. The fighting caused a large fire in a building on the site. The plant is the largest nuclear power station in Europe. Authorities said the fire was extinguished, and Russia kept control of the plant.

Russia's defence minister blamed the fire on a "monstrous attack" by Ukrainian saboteurs. Ukrainian emergency services later said the fire was in a building outside the power plant itself. The Zaporizhzhia military administration said radiation measurements remained unchanged and did not endanger the population, and Ukrainian emergency services described levels as within normal limits.

An official of Ukraine's operator Energoatom told Reuters that the plant was running normally with staff at their posts, but that Energoatom had lost contact with plant managers and oversight of radiation conditions after the takeover. The International Atomic Energy Agency said the fire did not affect essential equipment and that the situation was stable. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said the attacks compromised the plant's security, that the world was fortunate that no radiation was released, and that the situation was "fragile and unstable". He said he was in constant contact with Ukrainian authorities and might travel to Ukraine.
